statement: If there is a break in a wire, electric current will still flow up to the point of the break.
contrast_quote: A break anywhere in the loop stops the current in the whole loop.

statement: Electrons move through a circuit from the positive terminal to the negative terminal of a cell.
contrast_quote: The electrons move the opposite way, from the negative terminal to the positive terminal.

statement: To measure the current through a component, an ammeter must be connected in parallel across it.
contrast_quote: An ammeter must be connected in series with the component, so that all of the current flows through it.

statement: I believe that potential difference flows through the wires of a circuit just like electric charge does.
contrast_quote: It does not flow through a wire.

statement: I believe that a voltmeter must be connected in series with a component to measure its potential difference.
contrast_quote: A voltmeter must be connected in parallel, across the component being measured.

statement: I believe that a 9 V battery gives a total of 9 J of energy to the whole circuit regardless of how much charge passes through it.
contrast_quote: A 9 V battery gives 9 J to every coulomb that passes through it.

statement: A longer wire has less resistance to current than a shorter wire of the same material and thickness.
contrast_quote: A longer wire has a greater resistance than a shorter wire of the same material and thickness.

statement: Thicker wires offer more resistance to electric current than thinner wires of the same material and length.
contrast_quote: A thicker wire has a smaller resistance than a thinner wire of the same material and length.

statement: Heating up a metal wire causes its resistance to decrease because the energy helps charge move through it.
contrast_quote: The resistance of a metal wire rises when the wire gets hotter, because the atoms vibrate more and collide with more of the moving charge.

statement: Doubling the potential difference across a component while keeping the resistance constant will cause the current to drop by half.
contrast_quote: When the resistance stays constant, doubling the potential difference doubles the current.

statement: If you double the resistance in a component while keeping the potential difference constant, the current flowing through it will also double.
contrast_quote: When the potential difference stays constant, doubling the resistance halves the current.

statement: You can calculate the potential difference across a component if you only know the current flowing through it.
contrast_quote: To find any one of V, I or R, you must know the other two.

statement: I believe that electric current gets used up as it flows through components, making the current smaller after passing through a bulb.
contrast_quote: The current is the same at every point in a series circuit, because the charge has no other path to take and cannot pile up or disappear along the way.

statement: I believe that adding an extra resistor in series causes the current in the circuit to increase.
contrast_quote: Adding another resistor in series increases the total resistance, so the current in the circuit gets smaller.

statement: I believe that when components in a series circuit have different resistances, the component with the smaller resistance gets the larger share of the potential difference.
contrast_quote: If the resistances are different, the component with the larger resistance gets the larger share of the potential difference.
